name: National University of Singapore
header:
National University of Singapore
Singapore · Mathematics PhD (direct bachelor’s entry); MSc Mathematics by Research alternative
Canadian/Asian selection; not a US News graduate rank.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• 15 November 2026 is an explicit current-cycle deadline, only10days after this research date.
• Confirm letter completion before the programme deadline; the general system’s28days is not a confirmed
departmental grace period.
• Do not omit required SOP merely because optional personal statement appears in Math’s checklist.
• Updated English threshold conflicts with the 2027 poster; UChicago100%English instruction needs
documentary proof.
• NUS funding amounts are SGD; tuition waiver does not explicitly waive every miscellaneous or health fee.
• This is a broad fit shortlist, not every NUS mathematician. Tan Eng Chye is listed as professor and NUS
President; administrative role/current supervision not verified, so not treated as an ordinary adviser. Louis
Chen is emeritus. Current narrow-fit research for Victor Tan/Wing Keung To remains incomplete.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Direct PhD entry is possible with a four-year mathematics honours bachelor’s or equivalent; a master’s is not
mandatory. Science describes a relevant four-year degree averaging B as an example of equivalence, while its
preferred honours standard is Distinction or better. UChicago mathematics education is a plausible qualifying
background, subject to transcript/equivalence and competitive evaluation. MSc by Research is another route,
but the department gives preference to applicants intending a PhD. F-1 is not Singapore student status;
admission does not itself provide a Singapore Student’s Pass. Citizenship and final degree date still need to be
supplied. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s7] [s14] [s38]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose PhD or research MSc; review current faculty and indicate research areas. A specific thesis topic and
prior agreement from a supervisor are not mandatory under central FAQ. Gather transcript,
current-student/degree evidence, passport, English-medium proof, CV, statement, and two academic referees.
Select scholarship interest inside GradApp, check mandatory fields, send reference requests and pay the fee
before closing. Shortlisted scholarship applicants may be interviewed. No evidence of a mandatory
pre-application faculty interview. [s1] [s3] [s6] [s7]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Prior supervisor consent is not required by central FAQ; identifying research areas is useful and proposed
supervisor may be blank. Contact matching current faculty about research fit and 2027 capacity; no message
was sent. List below emphasizes AG/arithmetic geometry, complex geometry and representation/automorphic
theory. Broad dynamical/topological matches are included only where stated; university administrators and
stale publication records are flagged. [s6] [s15]
Portal workflow [Conflict]
Use GradApp at https://gradapp.nus.edu.sg/apply; public guide explains checklist, recommendations and
payment. Mandatory items are checked before submission; no applicant edits afterward, although central FAQ
allows case-by-case administrative unlocking for corrections. Math says upload PDFs and do not mail initial

documents; central older FAQ mentions10MB total and mailing oversized material - compress/check current
upload limits and ask Math instead of mailing by assumption. Confirm current field limits inside the
applicant-controlled portal; no account was created during research. [s1] [s6] [s7]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Explicit August 2027 Math poster confirms15November 2026 deadline; most detailed requirements remain
standing live web policies, scholarship rates effective 2026, and general portal guide last updated10December
2025. Do not mistake the poster’s 2025 file path for a 2026-only intake: its text expressly names 2027. [s1] [s2]
[s7] [s9]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
August 2027 PhD: application window 16 May-15 November 2026, explicitly printed in the Math poster. Exact
closing hour/timezone is not published there; confirm the GradApp listing and submit early in Singapore time.
January 2027: 1 January-15 May 2026, already closed. Research MSc follows the same Science standing 15
November/15 May schedule; no separately explicit 2027 MSc notice located. [s2] [s3]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
Apply for NUS Research Scholarship within the admission application by 15 November 2026 for August 2027.
Science Dean’s Fellowship uses the same 16 May-15 November previous-year window and selection from
Research Scholarship applicants. PGF requires faculty/department nomination; any internal nomination or
follow-up-document deadline is not publicly fixed. [s2] [s9] [s10] [s11]
Reference receipt [Conflict]
Unresolved conflict: Science requires all supporting documents by the application close and says an application
is incomplete without two reports, implying 15 November 2026 for a complete August 2027 file. The December
2025 general guide says each invitation carries 28 days and a reminder after expiry grants one additional
week. That system expiry is not proof the department accepts a late file. Obtain both by 15 November and ask
askmath-res@nus.edu.sg whether any later invitation date is honored. Invitation sample uses UTC+8;
programme closing hour remains unknown. [s3] [s4] [s7]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Applicable scores and English-medium proof are supporting documents due by 15 November 2026. No
Math-specific later ETS-receipt grace period located. Science gives TOEFL code 9087/department72 and
GRE0677/department0703. English tests must remain valid at the beginning of the relevant application period
(two-year validity); confirm current TOEFL scoring and report instructions if testing. [s1] [s3] [s4]
Supporting documents [2027 confirmed]
All supporting PDFs, translations where needed, application and payment must reach NUS by 15 November
2026; late/incomplete applications are not processed for that intake. Final degree certificate may follow the
current-student letter at application; exact post-offer original/degree-verification date is in
admission/onboarding instructions, not publicly fixed for Math 2027. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s7]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Reply through GradApp by the individual offer letter’s deadline; no universal 15 April commitment date is
published. Only one NUS programme may be accepted per intake. An acceptance fee, if required in that offer,
must also be paid; a Math-specific amount was not established. Science expects decisions by 31May;
Math/central FAQ says earlyJune for August entry, a small official discrepancy. [s1] [s3] [s6] [s7]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Updated Math FAQ: TOEFL5.0 on the new scale or95 on the old iBT scale, with old-scale writing minimum 22;
IELTS7.0. No corresponding new writing subsection threshold supplied. Science states two-year validity.
However the explicit 2027 Math poster still prints TOEFL85/IELTS6.0, and general NUS admissions calls English
tests optional whereas Math/Science FAQ requires proof if undergraduate teaching was not entirely English.
Use the English-medium exemption when documented; otherwise obtain written reconciliation before selecting
a test. Home editions, IELTS One Skill Retake, score combining and official-receipt grace are not established in
the Math sources. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Math and Science expressly allow documentary proof that the first degree’s instruction was100% English
instead of a test. A completed UChicago degree should meet that instructional-language condition (inference),
but supply official institutional evidence; USF-1 status alone is irrelevant. Exact acceptable document
issuer/template and treatment of an unfinished degree are not specified; obtain a UChicago registrar
English-medium letter and confirm with Math. Dean’s Fellowship likewise exempts English-taught
undergraduates. [s1] [s4] [s11]
GRE General [Conflict]
Strongly encouraged by the current Math page and 2027 poster; central research-admissions list calls it
optional and application-strengthening. Science FAQ contradicts itself: admission-requirements paragraph says
compulsory, later GRE question says strongly encouraged. Treat the department’s published position as the
best programme-specific evidence, but obtain written clarification if submitting without GRE. No Math-specific
minimum found; do not import Statistics’320/3.5 thresholds. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s5]
GRE Mathematics [Unresolved]
No separate Mathematics Subject GRE requirement or recommendation established in the PhD/research-MSc
pages. Their generic GRE language does not establish whether Subject scores substitute for General scores or
receive consideration. Coursework-MSc rules for nonmathematics applicants are a different programme; ask
Math before ordering a Subject report. [s1] [s4] [s14]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least two academic referees under the Math supporting-document checklist; Science specifically requires
receipt of two reports. General admissions also mentions professional referees, but academic mathematics
references are the programme-specific choice. Maximum accepted number and any mandated referee
relationship are not publicly confirmed. [s1] [s3] [s5]

Scholarship references [Unresolved]
The ordinary scholarship request is embedded in GradApp. No published additional referee count or distinct
referee questions were located for Research Scholarship or Science Dean’s Fellowship. PGF nomination can
lead to further instructions; do not assume those are identical or already satisfied. Exact current
recommendation form/questions remain portal-only. [s9] [s10] [s11]
What sends the invitation [Conflict]
December 2025 guide instructs applicants to enter an institutional/company email and press Send to
Recommender; that sends the report form. Entering details alone is not explicitly said to send it. The same
guide later describes invitations after application submission, so the exact interaction between early send and
automatic submission email needs live confirmation. [s7]
Before versus after submission [Conflict]
The guide explicitly says assigned referees receive an email after online submission, but its earlier Send to
Recommender control suggests an earlier send is possible. Do not interpret the later paragraph as an exclusive
after-submission-only rule. [s7]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
GradApp has an Application Checklist for missing information and a Recommendations page with reminder
controls; updates can take30-60minutes. The public text does not establish the precise Math report-received
label or an automatic applicant email for each letter. Check the individual recommendation status and
department completeness; Math says it does not separately acknowledge applications. [s1] [s7]
Updating and reusing letters [Conflict]
The older March 2024 guide shows excluding/replacing and reinstating a referee; the December 2025 guide
removes those sections and documents reminders only. Current replacement/edit rights therefore need
confirmation. Neither guide establishes replacement of a submitted letter, reuse across programmes/intakes,
or applicant access to letter contents. Some application fields prepopulate for other programmes; that is not
proof letters transfer. [s7] [s8]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required by central admissions and listed by Math. Prompt (faithful paraphrase): give a comprehensive
account of academic achievements and relevant experience. No public page/word/font limit located; upload
PDF under the applicable supporting-document field. Links alone are not stated to replace a CV. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required statement of purpose. Prompt (faithful paraphrase): explain research interests, career aims and
reasons for choosing the programme. Exact portal wording, word/page/character limit and font specifications
are not public. Supporting files are PDFs; verify whether the current programme requests an upload or text box
before drafting to a length. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Personal / background statement [Conflict]
Math checklist marks a personal statement optional; central statement of purpose is compulsory. These should
not be conflated. No separate adversity/background/diversity prompt or public length limit is supplied; confirm
whether the optional personal-statement upload is distinct from the SOP in the portal. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Required within SOP and research-area fields. Faithful paraphrase: identify the mathematical area you hope to
pursue; an exact thesis problem is unnecessary if not yet chosen. A proposed supervisor may be left blank
under central FAQ. No standalone length/format limit published. [s1] [s6] [s7]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
No full research proposal is listed for Mathematics; Science’s proposal item is explicitly for Chemistry. Research

area/SOP still required. No Math proposal template, word limit, formatting or upload/link rule established; do
not assume Chemistry’s requirement applies. [s3] [s6]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
No mandatory thesis/writing sample established. Math explicitly permits publications or abstracts as optional
research evidence. A separate unpublished thesis/research-summary upload, its limits and linking rules need
current-portal confirmation. [s1] [s3]
Publications list [Standing rule]
Publications or abstracts optional in Math checklist; central admissions treats research/publication evidence as
enhancing rather than compulsory. Guide includes publications/awards details. Upload permitted supporting
PDFs; no public cap, prescribed citation style or rule allowing URL-only substitution found. [s1] [s3] [s5] [s7]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
A separate mathematics-course inventory or course-description/syllabus upload is not listed for this Math
PhD/research-MSc route in the public checklist. Transcript is required. No standalone prompt, limit, or
upload/link permission for an extra course document was established; confirm the live programme-specific
supporting-document fields. [s1] [s3] [s7] [s14]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
Select Research Scholarship in GradApp. Dean’s Fellowship is awarded to qualified Research Scholarship
applicants; no separately published essay. PGF is by nomination and may require additional application
instructions if selected; exact additional prompts/limits/reference questions are not public. Commonwealth
scholarship also uses GradApp and requires qualifying nationality. Do not draft invented scholarship essays.
[s9] [s10] [s11] [s12]

Guide requests prior NUS applications, applications to other institutions, funding source, awards, and
employment/leadership/voluntary experience where relevant; employment section can be blank if none. No

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
NUS Research Scholarship international PhD rate effective1Jan 2026: SGD3000/month, plus SGD500/month
after QE, with full tuition waiver (12-month arithmetic SGD36000/42000 before/after QE). Math 2027 poster
additionally promises SGD500/month departmental allowance to recipients of scholarships other than PGF: if
applied to RS, arithmetic becomes SGD42000/48000 per12months; have the offer confirm stacking and
duration. Science Dean’s Fellowship: SGD3600/month (43200/year arithmetic) plus full tuition waiver. PGF:
SGD3900/month (46800/year arithmetic), full tuition waiver, international settlingSGD1000 and one-way
airfare up toSGD750; additional NUSGS monthly/research incentive amounts are not published. These
alternatives are not additive scholarships. Miscellaneous student/health fees and insurance costs are not
explicitly covered by the quoted tuition waiver. [s2] [s9] [s10] [s11]
Years of support [Conflict]
RS and PGF normally/maximally4years for PhD; RS research-MSc2years. Awards start for 1year and are then
renewable semester by semester on satisfactory progress under current central terms; Math’s page instead
says annual renewal. PhD maximum candidature5years; Math 2027 poster says fifth-year support may be
granted for merit/progress with departmental recommendation, not guaranteed. Summer months are implicit
in monthly scholarship payments, with exact leave/suspension conditions determined by award terms. [s1] [s2]
[s9] [s10] [s11]

International eligibility [Standing rule]
RS, PGF and Science Dean’s Fellowship explicitly accept all international nationalities. Citizenship-specific
Commonwealth funding requires citizenship of a qualifying Commonwealth country and excludes Singapore
citizens/PR; UChicago/F-1 does not determine that eligibility. Scholarships are competitive, not an automatic

National University of Singapore

Canadian/Asian selection; not a US News graduate rank.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• 15 November 2026 is an explicit current-cycle deadline, only10days after this research date.
• Confirm letter completion before the programme deadline; the general system’s28days is not a confirmed
departmental grace period.
• Do not omit required SOP merely because optional personal statement appears in Math’s checklist.
• Updated English threshold conflicts with the 2027 poster; UChicago100%English instruction needs
documentary proof.
• NUS funding amounts are SGD; tuition waiver does not explicitly waive every miscellaneous or health fee.
• This is a broad fit shortlist, not every NUS mathematician. Tan Eng Chye is listed as professor and NUS
President; administrative role/current supervision not verified, so not treated as an ordinary adviser. Louis
Chen is emeritus. Current narrow-fit research for Victor Tan/Wing Keung To remains incomplete.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Direct PhD entry is possible with a four-year mathematics honours bachelor’s or equivalent; a master’s is not
mandatory. Science describes a relevant four-year degree averaging B as an example of equivalence, while its
preferred honours standard is Distinction or better. UChicago mathematics education is a plausible qualifying
background, subject to transcript/equivalence and competitive evaluation. MSc by Research is another route,
but the department gives preference to applicants intending a PhD. F-1 is not Singapore student status;
admission does not itself provide a Singapore Student’s Pass. Citizenship and final degree date still need to be
supplied. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s7] [s14] [s38]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose PhD or research MSc; review current faculty and indicate research areas. A specific thesis topic and
prior agreement from a supervisor are not mandatory under central FAQ. Gather transcript,
current-student/degree evidence, passport, English-medium proof, CV, statement, and two academic referees.
Select scholarship interest inside GradApp, check mandatory fields, send reference requests and pay the fee
before closing. Shortlisted scholarship applicants may be interviewed. No evidence of a mandatory
pre-application faculty interview. [s1] [s3] [s6] [s7]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Prior supervisor consent is not required by central FAQ; identifying research areas is useful and proposed
supervisor may be blank. Contact matching current faculty about research fit and 2027 capacity; no message
was sent. List below emphasizes AG/arithmetic geometry, complex geometry and representation/automorphic
theory. Broad dynamical/topological matches are included only where stated; university administrators and
stale publication records are flagged. [s6] [s15]
Portal workflow [Conflict]
Use GradApp at https://gradapp.nus.edu.sg/apply; public guide explains checklist, recommendations and
payment. Mandatory items are checked before submission; no applicant edits afterward, although central FAQ
allows case-by-case administrative unlocking for corrections. Math says upload PDFs and do not mail initial

documents; central older FAQ mentions10MB total and mailing oversized material - compress/check current
upload limits and ask Math instead of mailing by assumption. Confirm current field limits inside the
applicant-controlled portal; no account was created during research. [s1] [s6] [s7]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Explicit August 2027 Math poster confirms15November 2026 deadline; most detailed requirements remain
standing live web policies, scholarship rates effective 2026, and general portal guide last updated10December
2025. Do not mistake the poster’s 2025 file path for a 2026-only intake: its text expressly names 2027. [s1] [s2]
[s7] [s9]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
August 2027 PhD: application window 16 May-15 November 2026, explicitly printed in the Math poster. Exact
closing hour/timezone is not published there; confirm the GradApp listing and submit early in Singapore time.
January 2027: 1 January-15 May 2026, already closed. Research MSc follows the same Science standing 15
November/15 May schedule; no separately explicit 2027 MSc notice located. [s2] [s3]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
Apply for NUS Research Scholarship within the admission application by 15 November 2026 for August 2027.
Science Dean’s Fellowship uses the same 16 May-15 November previous-year window and selection from
Research Scholarship applicants. PGF requires faculty/department nomination; any internal nomination or
follow-up-document deadline is not publicly fixed. [s2] [s9] [s10] [s11]
Reference receipt [Conflict]
Unresolved conflict: Science requires all supporting documents by the application close and says an application
is incomplete without two reports, implying 15 November 2026 for a complete August 2027 file. The December
2025 general guide says each invitation carries 28 days and a reminder after expiry grants one additional
week. That system expiry is not proof the department accepts a late file. Obtain both by 15 November and ask
askmath-res@nus.edu.sg whether any later invitation date is honored. Invitation sample uses UTC+8;
programme closing hour remains unknown. [s3] [s4] [s7]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
Applicable scores and English-medium proof are supporting documents due by 15 November 2026. No
Math-specific later ETS-receipt grace period located. Science gives TOEFL code 9087/department72 and
GRE0677/department0703. English tests must remain valid at the beginning of the relevant application period
(two-year validity); confirm current TOEFL scoring and report instructions if testing. [s1] [s3] [s4]
Supporting documents [2027 confirmed]
All supporting PDFs, translations where needed, application and payment must reach NUS by 15 November
2026; late/incomplete applications are not processed for that intake. Final degree certificate may follow the
current-student letter at application; exact post-offer original/degree-verification date is in
admission/onboarding instructions, not publicly fixed for Math 2027. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s7]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Reply through GradApp by the individual offer letter’s deadline; no universal 15 April commitment date is
published. Only one NUS programme may be accepted per intake. An acceptance fee, if required in that offer,
must also be paid; a Math-specific amount was not established. Science expects decisions by 31May;
Math/central FAQ says earlyJune for August entry, a small official discrepancy. [s1] [s3] [s6] [s7]

English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Updated Math FAQ: TOEFL5.0 on the new scale or95 on the old iBT scale, with old-scale writing minimum 22;
IELTS7.0. No corresponding new writing subsection threshold supplied. Science states two-year validity.
However the explicit 2027 Math poster still prints TOEFL85/IELTS6.0, and general NUS admissions calls English
tests optional whereas Math/Science FAQ requires proof if undergraduate teaching was not entirely English.
Use the English-medium exemption when documented; otherwise obtain written reconciliation before selecting
a test. Home editions, IELTS One Skill Retake, score combining and official-receipt grace are not established in
the Math sources. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Math and Science expressly allow documentary proof that the first degree’s instruction was100% English
instead of a test. A completed UChicago degree should meet that instructional-language condition (inference),
but supply official institutional evidence; USF-1 status alone is irrelevant. Exact acceptable document
issuer/template and treatment of an unfinished degree are not specified; obtain a UChicago registrar
English-medium letter and confirm with Math. Dean’s Fellowship likewise exempts English-taught
undergraduates. [s1] [s4] [s11]
GRE General [Conflict]
Strongly encouraged by the current Math page and 2027 poster; central research-admissions list calls it
optional and application-strengthening. Science FAQ contradicts itself: admission-requirements paragraph says
compulsory, later GRE question says strongly encouraged. Treat the department’s published position as the
best programme-specific evidence, but obtain written clarification if submitting without GRE. No Math-specific
minimum found; do not import Statistics’320/3.5 thresholds. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s5]
GRE Mathematics [Unresolved]
No separate Mathematics Subject GRE requirement or recommendation established in the PhD/research-MSc
pages. Their generic GRE language does not establish whether Subject scores substitute for General scores or
receive consideration. Coursework-MSc rules for nonmathematics applicants are a different programme; ask
Math before ordering a Subject report. [s1] [s4] [s14]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload university transcript; degree certificate, or official full-time-student-status letter while still enrolled;
passport identification page for international applicants; required test reports/English-medium evidence;
English translations for non-English documents. NUS does not request hardcopies at initial Math application. All
prior/postgraduate qualifications are entered if applicable. Exact final official-transcript authentication and
receipt deadline follows the offer. [s1] [s3] [s7]
Mathematics-course list; Course descriptions [Unresolved]

PhD/research-MSc route in the public checklist. Transcript is required. No standalone prompt, limit, or
upload/link permission for an extra course document was established; confirm the live programme-specific
supporting-document fields. [s1] [s3] [s7] [s14]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least two academic referees under the Math supporting-document checklist; Science specifically requires
receipt of two reports. General admissions also mentions professional referees, but academic mathematics
references are the programme-specific choice. Maximum accepted number and any mandated referee
relationship are not publicly confirmed. [s1] [s3] [s5]

Scholarship references [Unresolved]
The ordinary scholarship request is embedded in GradApp. No published additional referee count or distinct
referee questions were located for Research Scholarship or Science Dean’s Fellowship. PGF nomination can
lead to further instructions; do not assume those are identical or already satisfied. Exact current
recommendation form/questions remain portal-only. [s9] [s10] [s11]
What sends the invitation [Conflict]
December 2025 guide instructs applicants to enter an institutional/company email and press Send to
Recommender; that sends the report form. Entering details alone is not explicitly said to send it. The same
guide later describes invitations after application submission, so the exact interaction between early send and
automatic submission email needs live confirmation. [s7]
Before versus after submission [Conflict]
The guide explicitly says assigned referees receive an email after online submission, but its earlier Send to
Recommender control suggests an earlier send is possible. Do not interpret the later paragraph as an exclusive
after-submission-only rule. [s7]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
GradApp has an Application Checklist for missing information and a Recommendations page with reminder
controls; updates can take30-60minutes. The public text does not establish the precise Math report-received
label or an automatic applicant email for each letter. Check the individual recommendation status and
department completeness; Math says it does not separately acknowledge applications. [s1] [s7]
Updating and reusing letters [Conflict]
The older March 2024 guide shows excluding/replacing and reinstating a referee; the December 2025 guide
removes those sections and documents reminders only. Current replacement/edit rights therefore need
confirmation. Neither guide establishes replacement of a submitted letter, reuse across programmes/intakes,
or applicant access to letter contents. Some application fields prepopulate for other programmes; that is not
proof letters transfer. [s7] [s8]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required by central admissions and listed by Math. Prompt (faithful paraphrase): give a comprehensive
account of academic achievements and relevant experience. No public page/word/font limit located; upload
PDF under the applicable supporting-document field. Links alone are not stated to replace a CV. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required statement of purpose. Prompt (faithful paraphrase): explain research interests, career aims and
reasons for choosing the programme. Exact portal wording, word/page/character limit and font specifications
are not public. Supporting files are PDFs; verify whether the current programme requests an upload or text box
before drafting to a length. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Personal / background statement [Conflict]
Math checklist marks a personal statement optional; central statement of purpose is compulsory. These should
not be conflated. No separate adversity/background/diversity prompt or public length limit is supplied; confirm
whether the optional personal-statement upload is distinct from the SOP in the portal. [s1] [s3] [s5]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Required within SOP and research-area fields. Faithful paraphrase: identify the mathematical area you hope to
pursue; an exact thesis problem is unnecessary if not yet chosen. A proposed supervisor may be left blank
under central FAQ. No standalone length/format limit published. [s1] [s6] [s7]

not assume Chemistry’s requirement applies. [s3] [s6]

research evidence. A separate unpublished thesis/research-summary upload, its limits and linking rules need
current-portal confirmation. [s1] [s3]

Select Research Scholarship in GradApp. Dean’s Fellowship is awarded to qualified Research Scholarship
applicants; no separately published essay. PGF is by nomination and may require additional application
instructions if selected; exact additional prompts/limits/reference questions are not public. Commonwealth
scholarship also uses GradApp and requires qualifying nationality. Do not draft invented scholarship essays.

Guide requests prior NUS applications, applications to other institutions, funding source, awards, and
employment/leadership/voluntary experience where relevant; employment section can be blank if none. No

FAQ uses living funds ofS$18000/year plus tuition/miscellaneous fees as its proof threshold, not a reliable full
cost-of-living budget. [s6] [s7]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
NUS Research Scholarship international PhD rate effective1Jan 2026: SGD3000/month, plus SGD500/month
after QE, with full tuition waiver (12-month arithmetic SGD36000/42000 before/after QE). Math 2027 poster
additionally promises SGD500/month departmental allowance to recipients of scholarships other than PGF: if
applied to RS, arithmetic becomes SGD42000/48000 per12months; have the offer confirm stacking and
duration. Science Dean’s Fellowship: SGD3600/month (43200/year arithmetic) plus full tuition waiver. PGF:
SGD3900/month (46800/year arithmetic), full tuition waiver, international settlingSGD1000 and one-way
airfare up toSGD750; additional NUSGS monthly/research incentive amounts are not published. These
alternatives are not additive scholarships. Miscellaneous student/health fees and insurance costs are not
explicitly covered by the quoted tuition waiver. [s2] [s9] [s10] [s11]
Years of support [Conflict]
RS and PGF normally/maximally4years for PhD; RS research-MSc2years. Awards start for 1year and are then
renewable semester by semester on satisfactory progress under current central terms; Math’s page instead
says annual renewal. PhD maximum candidature5years; Math 2027 poster says fifth-year support may be
granted for merit/progress with departmental recommendation, not guaranteed. Summer months are implicit
in monthly scholarship payments, with exact leave/suspension conditions determined by award terms. [s1] [s2]
[s9] [s10] [s11]

International eligibility [Standing rule]
RS, PGF and Science Dean’s Fellowship explicitly accept all international nationalities. Citizenship-specific
Commonwealth funding requires citizenship of a qualifying Commonwealth country and excludes Singapore
citizens/PR; UChicago/F-1 does not determine that eligibility. Scholarships are competitive, not an automatic
funding guarantee for every admitted student. [s9] [s10] [s11] [s12] [s38]

Maintain satisfactory academic/research progress; RS forbids unapproved employment or concurrent awards.
International recipients perform Graduate Assistantship duties. PGF specifies312 total teaching hours; Dean’s
Fellowship416hours. Exact RS work-hour table requires its terms/department confirmation. These scholarships
list no specific postgraduation service bond; assistantship obligations still apply. Tuition subsidy eligibility and
separate award undertakings must be checked before acceptance. [s9] [s10] [s11] [s12] [s13]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Indicate Research Scholarship within admission application. Dean’s Fellowship selected through that
application; PGF requires department/faculty nomination with later instructions, and Lee Kong Chian-funded
PGF emphasizes leadership/community service. No public independent Math 2027 scholarship essay/deadline
beyond this process found. [s9] [s10] [s11]

Commonwealth Scholarship if eligible: SGD3000/month PhD or2900/month research MSc, tuition subsidy,

pure AG/number-theory project eligibility and any bond must be verified for the specific scheme, not assumed.
PGF/Dean’s awards are alternative higher awards. Department may recommend fifth-year support. [s1] [s2] [s10]
[s11] [s12]
Application fee [Standing rule]
SGD50 per application including GST, nonrefundable; must be paid by programme closing. December 2025
guide supports Visa, Mastercard, American Express or PayNow. Older guide additionally listed Alipay; use
current payment screen rather than assume it remains available. [s1] [s3] [s7] [s8]

No public need-based/international Math research application fee-waiver procedure, qualifying categories,
request deadline or fee-waiver code found in programme/Science/central sources and targeted search. Ask
askmath-res@nus.edu.sg before paying; do not infer a waiver from the guide’s generic “if any” fee wording.
